/-!
# The integer atomic floor of the canonical Weil measure

The floor of every actual singleton mass defines a dominated integer-valued atomic submeasure.
Its complement is a positive measure with every atom below one. Exact subtraction is proved on
finite-mass measurable sets by restricting before invoking finite measure cancellation. No
atomicity, discreteness, or total-mass assumption on the canonical source is supplied.
-/

open Set Filter MeasureTheory
open scoped ENNReal Topology
noncomputable section
namespace RHTower.WeilSpectral

/-- Integer part of the actual canonical singleton mass. -/
def quantizationIntegerWeight {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hW : WeilPositiveFull lam) (r : ℝ) : ℕ :=
  ⌊(boundaryMeasure hW).real {r}⌋₊

/-- The canonical integer atomic floor, with no atomicity assumption on the source. -/
def quantizationIntegerMeasure {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hW : WeilPositiveFull lam) : Measure ℝ :=
  Measure.sum fun r : ℝ => (quantizationIntegerWeight hW r : ℝ≥0∞) • Measure.dirac r

/-- Positive residual measure after removal of the actual integer atomic floor. -/
def quantizationResidualMeasure {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hW : WeilPositiveFull lam) : Measure ℝ :=
  boundaryMeasure hW - quantizationIntegerMeasure hW

theorem quantizationIntegerWeight_le {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hW : WeilPositiveFull lam) (r : ℝ) :
    (quantizationIntegerWeight hW r : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ boundaryMeasure hW {r} := by
  calc
    (quantizationIntegerWeight hW r : ℝ≥0∞) =
        ENNReal.ofReal (quantizationIntegerWeight hW r : ℝ) := by simp
    _ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ((boundaryMeasure hW).real {r}) :=
      ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal (Nat.floor_le ENNReal.toReal_nonneg)
    _ ≤ boundaryMeasure hW {r} := ENNReal.ofReal_toReal_le

theorem quantizationIntegerMeasure_apply {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hW : WeilPositiveFull lam)
    {s : Set ℝ} (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    quantizationIntegerMeasure hW s =
      ∑' r : ℝ, ((s.indicator (quantizationIntegerWeight hW) r : ℕ) : ℝ≥0∞) := by
  classical
  rw [quantizationIntegerMeasure, Measure.sum_apply _ hs]
  apply tsum_congr
  intro r
  by_cases hr : r ∈ s <;> simp [Measure.smul_apply, hr]

theorem quantizationIntegerMeasure_le {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hW : WeilPositiveFull lam) :
    quantizationIntegerMeasure hW ≤ boundaryMeasure hW := by
  classical
  refine Measure.le_iff.mpr fun s hs => ?_
  rw [quantizationIntegerMeasure_apply hW hs, ENNReal.tsum_eq_iSup_sum]
  refine iSup_le fun F => ?_
  calc
    ∑ r ∈ F, ((s.indicator (quantizationIntegerWeight hW) r : ℕ) : ℝ≥0∞) ≤
        ∑ r ∈ F, (boundaryMeasure hW).restrict s {r} := by
      apply Finset.sum_le_sum
      intro r _
      by_cases hr : r ∈ s
      · simpa [Measure.restrict_apply (measurableSet_singleton r),
          singleton_inter_of_mem hr, hr] using quantizationIntegerWeight_le hW r
      · simp [hr, Measure.restrict_apply (measurableSet_singleton r),
          singleton_inter_of_notMem hr]
    _ = (boundaryMeasure hW).restrict s (F : Set ℝ) := sum_measure_singleton
    _ ≤ (boundaryMeasure hW).restrict s univ := measure_mono (subset_univ _)
    _ = boundaryMeasure hW s := by simp

theorem quantizationIntegerMeasure_singleton {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hW : WeilPositiveFull lam) (r : ℝ) :
    quantizationIntegerMeasure hW {r} = (quantizationIntegerWeight hW r : ℝ≥0∞) :=
  Measure.sum_smul_dirac_singleton

/-- Finite source mass forces a finite sum of natural-valued atomic weights. -/
theorem quantizationIntegerMeasure_nat {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hW : WeilPositiveFull lam)
    {s : Set ℝ} (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hfin : boundaryMeasure hW s ≠ ∞) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, quantizationIntegerMeasure hW s = n := by
  classical
  let f : ℝ → ℕ := s.indicator (quantizationIntegerWeight hW)
  have hf : ∑' r : ℝ, (f r : ℝ≥0∞) ≠ ∞ := by
    rw [← quantizationIntegerMeasure_apply hW hs]
    exact ne_top_of_le_ne_top hfin (quantizationIntegerMeasure_le hW s)
  have hF : (Function.support f).Finite := by
    apply (ENNReal.finite_const_le_of_tsum_ne_top hf (one_ne_zero : (1 : ℝ≥0∞) ≠ 0)).subset
    intro r hr
    change (1 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ (f r : ℝ≥0∞)
    exact_mod_cast Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.mpr hr
  refine ⟨∑ r ∈ hF.toFinset, f r, ?_⟩
  rw [quantizationIntegerMeasure_apply hW hs]
  change (∑' r : ℝ, (f r : ℝ≥0∞)) = ((∑ r ∈ hF.toFinset, f r : ℕ) : ℝ≥0∞)
  rw [tsum_eq_sum (s := hF.toFinset)]
  · simp
  · intro r hr
    have hz : f r = 0 := by simpa using hr
    simp [hz]

theorem quantizationResidualMeasure_le {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hW : WeilPositiveFull lam) :
    quantizationResidualMeasure hW ≤ boundaryMeasure hW := Measure.sub_le

/-- The subtraction identity is paid locally, where the integer floor is finite. -/
theorem quantizationResidualMeasure_add_integer {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hW : WeilPositiveFull lam)
    {s : Set ℝ} (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hfin : boundaryMeasure hW s ≠ ∞) :
    quantizationResidualMeasure hW s + quantizationIntegerMeasure hW s = boundaryMeasure hW s := by
  let μ := boundaryMeasure hW

/-!
# Navier-Stokes torus-covering Haar invariance

This file extracts the Haar-average assertion (6.19) in Lemma 6.2 of the supplied
Navier-Stokes paper.  The corpus already proves that every nonsingular integer matrix pushes
normalized torus Haar measure to itself.  We expose the corresponding Bochner-integral
invariance and specialize it to the paper's matrix

`Jg = !![3, 1; 1, 5]`, whose determinant is `14`.
-/

open MeasureTheory

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.NavierStokesTorusHaarCovering

noncomputable section

variable {k : Type*} [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k]
variable {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]

/-- Pushforward by a nonsingular integer torus endomorphism preserves normalized Haar measure. -/
theorem map_torusIntegerHom_haar {N : Matrix k k ℤ} (hdet : N.det ≠ 0) :
    Measure.map (torusIntegerHom (N : k → k → ℤ))
        (finiteTorusHaarProbabilityMeasure k : Measure (UnitAddTorus k)) =
      (finiteTorusHaarProbabilityMeasure k : Measure (UnitAddTorus k)) := by
  have hmap := congrArg (fun μ : ProbabilityMeasure (UnitAddTorus k) =>
    (μ : Measure (UnitAddTorus k))) (orbitClosureHaar_eq_haar hdet)
  simpa [orbitClosureHaar, ProbabilityMeasure.toMeasure_map] using hmap

/-- **Lemma 6.2, Haar-average form.** Pullback by a nonsingular integer torus
endomorphism preserves every strongly measurable Bochner integral. -/
theorem integral_comp_torusIntegerHom {N : Matrix k k ℤ} (hdet : N.det ≠ 0)
    (f : UnitAddTorus k → F)
    (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f
      (finiteTorusHaarProbabilityMeasure k : Measure (UnitAddTorus k))) :
    (∫ x, f (torusIntegerHom (N : k → k → ℤ) x)
        ∂(finiteTorusHaarProbabilityMeasure k : Measure (UnitAddTorus k))) =
      ∫ x, f x
        ∂(finiteTorusHaarProbabilityMeasure k : Measure (UnitAddTorus k)) := by
  let μ := (finiteTorusHaarProbabilityMeasure k : Measure (UnitAddTorus k))
  have hfmap : AEStronglyMeasurable f
      (Measure.map (torusIntegerHom (N : k → k → ℤ)) μ) := by
    rw [map_torusIntegerHom_haar hdet]
    exact hf
  calc
    (∫ x, f (torusIntegerHom (N : k → k → ℤ) x) ∂μ) =
        ∫ x, f x ∂Measure.map (torusIntegerHom (N : k → k → ℤ)) μ :=
      (integral_map (continuous_torusIntegerHom (N : k → k → ℤ)).aemeasurable hfmap).symm
    _ = ∫ x, f x ∂μ := by rw [map_torusIntegerHom_haar hdet]

/-- Integer covering matrix `Jg` from equation (6.2). -/
def navierStokesCoverMatrix : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℤ :=
  !![3, 1; 1, 5]

/-- The paper's covering has degree fourteen. -/
theorem det_navierStokesCoverMatrix : navierStokesCoverMatrix.det = 14 := by
  norm_num [navierStokesCoverMatrix, Matrix.det_fin_two]

/-- Every iterated covering in Lemma 6.2 remains nonsingular. -/
theorem det_pow_navierStokesCoverMatrix_ne_zero (n : ℕ) :
    (navierStokesCoverMatrix ^ n).det ≠ 0 := by
  rw [Matrix.det_pow, det_navierStokesCoverMatrix]
  exact pow_ne_zero n (by norm_num)

/-- **Equation (6.19).** Haar averages agree after pullback by every power of the paper's
degree-fourteen torus covering. -/
theorem integral_comp_navierStokesCoverMatrix_pow (n : ℕ)
    (f : UnitAddTorus (Fin 2) → F)
    (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f
      (finiteTorusHaarProbabilityMeasure (Fin 2) : Measure (UnitAddTorus (Fin 2)))) :
    (∫ x, f (torusIntegerHom
        ((navierStokesCoverMatrix ^ n : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℤ) : Fin 2 → Fin 2 → ℤ) x)
        ∂(finiteTorusHaarProbabilityMeasure (Fin 2) : Measure (UnitAddTorus (Fin 2)))) =
      ∫ x, f x
        ∂(finiteTorusHaarProbabilityMeasure (Fin 2) : Measure (UnitAddTorus (Fin 2))) := by
  exact integral_comp_torusIntegerHom (det_pow_navierStokesCoverMatrix_ne_zero n) f hf

end

/-!
# Return volume of an integer character embedding

The completed time of a finite frequency packet is the image of a presenting torus under the
integer character matrix of the packet.  This file computes the order of the Haar volume of the
pulled-back return target.

A nonsingular integer square matrix pushes torus Haar measure to itself — its Fourier coefficients
are those of Haar because a nonsingular matrix has trivial left kernel — so preimages along it have
unchanged measure.  The pulled-back return target contains a ball of radius proportional to the
tolerance, because every character is Lipschitz with the constant given by its row sum, and it is
contained in the preimage of a ball of radius twice the tolerance along any nonsingular square
selection of characters.  Both bounds are of order `ε` to the presenting dimension, so the
logarithmic return exponent is exactly that dimension.
-/

open Filter MeasureTheory Metric Set Topology
open scoped BigOperators

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

variable {k : Type*} [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k]

/-- A nonsingular integer matrix has trivial left kernel. -/
theorem integerVecMul_eq_zero_iff {N : Matrix k k ℤ} (hdet : N.det ≠ 0) (n : k → ℤ) :
    (fun j => ∑ i, n i * N i j) = 0 ↔ n = 0 := by
  constructor
  · intro hn
    exact Matrix.eq_zero_of_vecMul_eq_zero hdet hn
  · rintro rfl
    funext j
    simp

/-- **A nonsingular integer matrix preserves torus Haar measure.**  Its pushforward has the Fourier
coefficients of Haar measure. -/
theorem orbitClosureHaar_eq_haar {N : Matrix k k ℤ} (hdet : N.det ≠ 0) :
    orbitClosureHaar (N : k → k → ℤ) = finiteTorusHaarProbabilityMeasure k := by
  refine probabilityMeasure_ext_of_mFourier_integral_eq _ _ fun n => ?_
  rw [orbitClosureHaar_mFourier_integral, finiteTorusHaarProbabilityMeasure_mFourier_integral,
    if_congr (integerVecMul_eq_zero_iff hdet n) rfl rfl]

/-- Preimages along a nonsingular integer torus endomorphism have unchanged Haar measure. -/
theorem measure_preimage_torusIntegerHom {N : Matrix k k ℤ} (hdet : N.det ≠ 0)
    {A : Set (UnitAddTorus k)} (hA : MeasurableSet A) :
    (finiteTorusHaarProbabilityMeasure k : Measure (UnitAddTorus k))
        (torusIntegerHom (N : k → k → ℤ) ⁻¹' A)
      = (finiteTorusHaarProbabilityMeasure k : Measure (UnitAddTorus k)) A := by
  have hmap := congrArg (fun μ : ProbabilityMeasure (UnitAddTorus k) =>
    (μ : Measure (UnitAddTorus k))) (orbitClosureHaar_eq_haar hdet)
  simp only [orbitClosureHaar, ProbabilityMeasure.toMeasure_map] at hmap
  rw [← Measure.map_apply (continuous_torusIntegerHom (N : k → k → ℤ)).measurable hA, hmap]

variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d]

/-- A crude uniform bound for the row sums of an integer character matrix. -/
def torusRowBound (M : d → k → ℤ) : ℝ := 1 + ∑ i, ∑ j, ‖M i j‖

omit [DecidableEq k] in
theorem one_le_torusRowBound (M : d → k → ℤ) : 1 ≤ torusRowBound M := by
  have : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ∑ i, ∑ j, ‖M i j‖ :=
    Finset.sum_nonneg fun _ _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun _ _ => norm_nonneg _
  simp only [torusRowBound]
  linarith

omit [DecidableEq k] in
theorem torusRowBound_pos (M : d → k → ℤ) : 0 < torusRowBound M :=
  lt_of_lt_of_le one_pos (one_le_torusRowBound M)

omit [DecidableEq k] in
theorem rowSum_le_torusRowBound (M : d → k → ℤ) (i : d) :
    ∑ j, ‖M i j‖ ≤ torusRowBound M := by
  have hmem : (∑ j, ‖M i j‖) ≤ ∑ i', ∑ j, ‖M i' j‖ :=
    Finset.single_le_sum (f := fun i' => ∑ j, ‖M i' j‖)
      (fun _ _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun _ _ => norm_nonneg _) (Finset.mem_univ i)
  simp only [torusRowBound]
  linarith

/-- The pulled-back anchored return target of an integer character family. -/
def integerReturnPreimage (M : d → k → ℤ) (ε : ℝ) : Set (UnitAddTorus k) :=
  {u | ∀ i, dist (torusIntegerHom M u i) 0 ≤ ε}

/-- The square character matrix selected by an index injection. -/
def selectedSquare (M : d → k → ℤ) (σ : k → d) : Matrix k k ℤ :=
  Matrix.of fun a b => M (σ a) b

omit [DecidableEq k] in
/-- Every character is Lipschitz with its row-sum constant, so a small ball lies in the pulled-back
return target. -/
theorem ball_subset_integerReturnPreimage (M : d → k → ℤ) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    Metric.ball (0 : UnitAddTorus k) (ε / torusRowBound M) ⊆ integerReturnPreimage M ε := by
  intro u hu
  have hL : 0 < torusRowBound M := torusRowBound_pos M
  have hr : 0 < ε / torusRowBound M := div_pos hε hL
  have hcoord : ∀ j, ‖u j‖ < ε / torusRowBound M := by
    have hall := (dist_pi_lt_iff hr).mp (mem_ball.mp hu)
    intro j
    simpa [dist_zero_right] using hall j
  intro i
  have hnorm : ‖torusIntegerHom M u i‖ ≤ ∑ j, ‖M i j‖ * ‖u j‖ := by
    refine le_trans (norm_sum_le _ _) (Finset.sum_le_sum fun j _ => ?_)
    exact norm_zsmul_le (M i j) (u j)

/-!
# Above the Euler edge the source is an honest random finite integer

The occupancy probabilities of the diagonal activation law are summable above the Euler edge, so
the first Borel--Cantelli lemma puts full mass on the configurations with only finitely many
occupied primes.  The source there is a random finite integer, and its radical is a finite
squarefree number.

This is the exact complement of the critical statement: at the Euler edge the same Kolmogorov
product is supported on configurations occupying infinitely many primes, so the finite-integer
carrier disappears precisely at the edge.
-/

open scoped BigOperators ENNReal NNReal

/-! ### The subcritical product law -/

/-- Subcritical Euler parameter `q_p = p ^ (-σ)`. -/
def subcriticalEulerParameter {σ : ℝ} (hσ : 1 < σ) (p : Nat.Primes) : unitInterval :=
  ⟨((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (-σ), by
    have hp : (1 : ℝ) ≤ ((p : ℕ) : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast p.2.one_lt.le
    refine ⟨Real.rpow_nonneg (by linarith) _, ?_⟩
    exact Real.rpow_le_one_of_one_le_of_nonpos hp (by linarith)⟩

theorem subcriticalEulerParameter_coe {σ : ℝ} (hσ : 1 < σ) (p : Nat.Primes) :
    (subcriticalEulerParameter hσ p : ℝ) = ((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (-σ) := rfl

/-- Kolmogorov product of the subcritical local activation laws. -/
def subcriticalEulerProductMeasure {σ : ℝ} (hσ : 1 < σ) :
    MeasureTheory.Measure CriticalEulerConfiguration :=
  MeasureTheory.Measure.infinitePi fun p : Nat.Primes ↦
    diagonalActivationMeasure (subcriticalEulerParameter hσ p)

instance subcriticalEulerProductMeasure_isProbabilityMeasure {σ : ℝ} (hσ : 1 < σ) :
    MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure (subcriticalEulerProductMeasure hσ) := by
  rw [subcriticalEulerProductMeasure]
  infer_instance

/-- The subcritical occupancy cylinder mass. -/
theorem subcriticalEulerProductMeasure_criticalPrimeOccupied {σ : ℝ} (hσ : 1 < σ)
    (p : Nat.Primes) :
